title: Fiji-Tonga supplied 15 of 17 late net event counts near 82 selected deep earthquakes in 2001-2024
abstract: We tested the geographic spread of a published late event excess near deep earthquakes. We reused a frozen USGS ComCat subset. Centers have depth greater than 300 km, magnitude 6.5 to below 8 and origin years 2001-2024. A one-year isolation rule on both sides retains 82 centers. M5+ neighbors within a depth-aware 200 km distance gave 29 after and 12 before counts on days 7-30. Fiji-Tonga supplied 15 of the 17 net counts from 29 centers. The other 53 centers gave four after and two before counts. Their excess rate was 0.00164 per center per day, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of -0.00136 to 0.00494. Intervals outside Fiji-Tonga also included zero at 100 km, 300 km and M5.5. Single-center deletion left positive point estimates. Thus broad regional concentration can remain when no single center dominates. This is a scope check on existing data, not independent confirmation or proof of a regional physical cause. Sparse counts, chosen boxes, mixed magnitude types, selection and incomplete dependence models limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, an independent scalar audit and a figure are included. External records are regenerated outside the signed draft.

display.caption: Broad-region late counts and region deletion estimates. Lines show conditional 95% three-year block intervals. The test uses 82 both-side isolated deep centers in 2001-2024.
